rules.title: Service registry key can be modified by non-admins
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: Whoever can write a service's registry key can change its ImagePath (or a svchost service's Parameters\ServiceDll) to their own program, which the service then runs as its account, usually SYSTEM, the next time it starts or the machine reboots.
rules.fix: Restore the default permissions on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<service> so only SYSTEM and Administrators can write it (sc sdset <service> <sddl>, or reset it to match a known-good machine). Find out what loosened it.

rules.title: Execution-hook registry key can be modified by non-admins
rules.subject: {category}: {key}
rules.why: Write access to this key lets a non-admin set an execution hook from scratch (an IFEO debugger, an AppInit or AppCert DLL, a Winlogon or Active Setup program, or an LSA / print-monitor / netsh DLL), which Windows then runs in a privileged context. Nothing needs to be hooked today for this to be exploitable.
rules.fix: Restore the default permissions so only SYSTEM and Administrators can write the key. These keys should never be writable by Users.

rules.title: Machine-wide Run key can be modified by non-admins
rules.subject: {key}
rules.why: Write access to a machine-wide Run key lets a non-admin add a program that starts in every user's session at logon, administrators included.
rules.fix: Restore the default permissions so only SYSTEM and Administrators can write HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run (and RunOnce, and the Wow6432Node copy).
